findings.reason: with s37 linked, dispatch order and scope for §38 are settled; without it the node's gate is unmeasurable and the work is likely duplicated.
findings.text: §38's done-when ("a read-back after repair in which §37's audit reports no live, non-derived, non-orphan name without a DD source", `:249`) needs §37's check to exist, but the s38 section element declares `data-links="sn-integrity-backlog#s35,sn-integrity-backlog#s36"` — §37 is absent, so a node dispatched on §38 before §37 has no instrument for the measure its gate names and will either block or silently implement §37's audit itself, outside its scope

findings.reason: the control decides whether the census's counts can be believed at all, and the plan's own §30 sets the precedent the node would otherwise not follow.
findings.text: §35's census is the sole input to §36's writer list and §38's repair list, yet its done-when requires only that the fragment place every name in exactly one population and names no positive control, unlike the sibling census §30, which requires a witness for each exclusion branch and states "the instrument proves it can see the population as well as the gap" (`:215`) — a query blind to one direction of `PRODUCED_NAME`, or to `origin`, reports a small or empty population and reads as a clean census, and §36 and §38 then work from a wrong list

findings.reason: the census's scope sentence and its three-population partition disagree, so the node chooses an interpretation that changes both the census counts and §38's worklist.
findings.text: §35 counts 264 sourceless live names and states two are derived parents "which legitimately have none", then defines three populations (orphans awaiting retirement, dropped edges, never bound) over which the done-when requires "every sourceless live name in exactly one"; the two derived parents fit none of the three under §37's own reading (which excludes derived explicitly, `:245`). If the node instead folds them into "never bound", §38 — "Restore each dropped or never-bound source §35 lists" (`:249`) — would attempt a restoration for a name whose sourcelessness is by design

findings.reason: a name the lifecycle would retire can be classified outside §35's orphan population and then block a WEST release, or send §38 to restore a source for a name that will be retired anyway.
findings.text: §35 defines its first population as "Orphans awaiting retirement: exhausted, with a live successor that holds the sources", but the operation it cites as "§31's orphan lifecycle (`supersede_exhausted_orphan` in `graph_ops.py`)" retires on `name_stage = 'exhausted' AND origin <> 'derived' AND NOT EXISTS {(:StandardNameSource)-[:PRODUCED_NAME]->(name)}` with no successor clause (`imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py:22634-22641`, applied at `:22778-22786`): the added clause is not in the cited mechanism, and §37 keys its release refusal on "not an orphan awaiting retirement, the population §35 separates", so the population the release gate spares differs from the population the lifecycle retires

findings.reason: the node must either invent the release-gate surface or add the plumbing the section implies (a second deliverable), and without the caller named the check can pass its own test while the release is unaffected.
findings.text: §37 says "the standard-name audits gain a check ... The release gate refuses while the check reports any name" and names no module, function or caller, unlike every sibling section (`:203` names `export.py`, `:207` names the file and line); the audits' only existing consumers are the pool validation and quarantine paths in `imas_codex/standard_names/workers.py:5097` and `:5165`, which pass `run_audits` issues to `has_critical_audit_failure` — no release gate reads them, so the done-when ("a test drives the release gate ... asserts the gate refuses and names it") is satisfiable by a gate nothing in the release path calls

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited `sn-review-through-jev` §5 resolves (its `s5` section exists and `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-review-through-jev/srtj-refine-ab-run.html:132` carries the 62-of-104 figure), and `supersede_exhausted_orphan` resolves in `imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py:22655,22792`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §35's census declares no control that its instrument can see each of the three populations it excludes into; a blind classifier reports a clean census.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every new unit names its fragment under `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/` (§35 `:237`, §36 `:241`, §37 `:245`, §38 `:249`), which is the plan's durable evidence directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or changelog prose reach the new section text, the fragment filenames or any symbol.
rubric_items.reasoning: findings — §35's three populations do not cover the 264 names its own measurement counts, and §37 names no file or caller for the audit it extends or the gate that must refuse.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of §35–§38 carries one deliverable (a census, a writer fix, an audit gate, a repair), and each done-when closes on that one.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §38's done-when runs §37's audit as its read-back, but §38's section element declares links to s35 and s36 only (`plan.html:248`, done-when at `:249`).
